meta.sourceNote: Every category and checklist item here is drawn directly from two source documents: the department's Scholarship Statement and the excerpted Faculty Handbook sections (3.9, 4.1, 4.8-4.11, 4.17.3). Where the source text is quoted, it's marked as a quote below so it's easy to point back to the original.

scholarshipCategories.name: Scholarship of Discovery
scholarshipCategories.summary: New knowledge in computing -- core or interdisciplinary -- disseminated in a recognized way.
evidenceForms: Research initiatives that push the boundaries of computing
Work that integrates student involvement
Dissemination via peer-reviewed journals, conferences, local forums, or creative presentations (tech-focused performances/exhibitions)
New terms, frameworks, or languages (programming-specific or interdisciplinary)

scholarshipCategories.name: Scholarship of Teaching and Learning
scholarshipCategories.summary: Research into how to teach computing well, or substantive curriculum development.
evidenceForms: Researching the efficacy of teaching tools
Strategies for integrating technology into the classroom
Methods to improve student engagement
Creation of new courses/programs, or significant overhaul of existing ones
Taking courses from other institutions to integrate new knowledge into teaching
Presentation at venues such as ACM SIGCSE, GDC, or local educational forums

scholarshipCategories.name: Scholarship of Integration
scholarshipCategories.summary: Computing in conversation with other disciplines.
evidenceForms: Collaboration with faculty in other disciplines (e.g. biology, economics, social sciences) to analyze/interpret data
Publications, conference presentations, or other recognition from such collaboration
Independent/singular research on interdisciplinary themes: information literacy, misinformation studies, visualization

scholarshipCategories.name: Scholarship of Application and Engagement
evidenceForms: Consulting with companies / contributing to real-world problems
Presenting research to industry groups
Presentations at industry meetings, community workshops, or other public engagement
Engagement with professional computing organizations (national/regional associations)
Committee work, conference presentations, or collaborative projects within those organizations

scholarshipCategories.name: Scholarship of Historiography
scholarshipCategories.source: Scholarship Statement (department extension to Boyer's model)
scholarshipCategories.summary: The history and cultural impact of computing.
evidenceForms: Study of the development of computing technologies, key figures, or social/ethical/cultural context
Academic papers or books
Creative works: plays, screenplays, performances

scholarshipCategories.name: Supporting Underrepresented Students in Research
scholarshipCategories.source: Scholarship Statement (department extension to Boyer's model)
scholarshipCategories.summary: Recruiting and mentoring underrepresented students in meaningful research.
evidenceForms: Actively recruiting and mentoring students from diverse backgrounds into research
Research projects reflecting/contributing to equity and inclusion in STEM
Resulting presentations, publications, or other external recognition

scholarshipEvidenceTypesQuote: Scholarship requires an external product that could include publication, public presentation of work at a conference or event, report to a public or private organization, or performance to a public audience. (Handbook 4.8.2)
scholarshipFlexibilityNote: Faculty members are not required to demonstrate contributions in all areas of scholarship for tenure or promotion. Significant achievements or substantial work in one or more areas can fulfill scholarship expectations... excellence in one domain can compensate for less activity in others. (Scholarship Statement, “Flexibility in Scholarship Areas”)

serviceCategories.name: Committees
serviceCategories.quote: Service on College, faculty, divisional, and departmental committees is a significant responsibility of faculty members. (4.8.3)

serviceCategories.name: Required events
serviceCategories.quote: Faculty attendance at the New Student Convocation, Honors Convocation, Baccalaureate, and Commencement is also required. (4.8.3)

serviceCategories.name: Requested occasions
serviceCategories.quote: Attendance at Chapel, service as an advisor to student organizations, attendance at athletic events, performances, recitals, lectures, Parents Weekend, Homecoming events, and participation in recruiting activities...may be requested on specific occasions by the Provost. (4.8.3)

serviceCategories.name: Academic advising
serviceCategories.quote: In the spring of their first year, after they have declared a major, they are assigned a faculty advisor from their major field of study. (4.8.4)

serviceCategories.name: Student org. advising
serviceCategories.quote: Each recognized student organization is required to have at least one faculty or staff advisor. (4.8.5)

serviceCategories.name: Outside the College
serviceCategories.quote: It is recognized that faculty members fulfill service responsibilities through participation in community and non-profit organizations outside the College community. (4.8.3)

teachingEssentials: Course description and syllabus for each class
Verifying class rosters with the Registrar
Identifying students with low grades and/or poor attendance
Submitting final grades to the Registrar
teachingEssentialsQuote: Certain activities on the part of faculty members are essential. These include but are not limited to: developing a course description and syllabus for each class; preparing regularly for class; maintaining office hours; verifying class rosters with the Registrar; identifying students with low grades and/or poor attendance; submitting final grades to the Registrar; and advising students. (4.8.1)
chairObservationQuote: The Department Chair/Program Director visits all tenure-track and annual/multi-year faculty members at mutually agreed times, at least once per year. (4.9.1)
studentEvalsQuote: [The Chair] receives copies of the compilation of student evaluations for all courses taught in the department or program each term. (4.9.1)
tenureFileChecklist: Letter of Recommendation from Dean at Carthage
Letter of Recommendation from Chair at Carthage
tenureFileChecklistQuote: In consideration of a candidate for tenure, the following documents are required of all candidates: 1. The Candidate Narrative...2. A current CV. 3. Letters of Recommendation... 4. Departmental Scholarship Statement. 5. Additional Supporting Materials... 6. Course Evaluations. (4.10.2)

threeAreasQuote: The work of a faculty member includes teaching, scholarship and professional activities, and involvement in the College and larger community. Excellence in performing these responsibilities is the primary criterion for reappointment, tenure, promotion, and level of compensation. (4.8)
